headline: ATO increasing scrutiny of SMSFs with penalties including personal taxation of unauthorised benefit payments
reasoning: Marjon Muizer of Red Willow Super notes the ATO is cracking down on SMSFs with increased scrutiny around fund expenses and asset valuations. In one example, a trustee spent $25,000 on a forex trading course from a $100,000 fund — roughly a quarter of fund assets — and the ATO treated this as an early release benefit (member lump sum) taxed at 20% plus Medicare levy, regardless of subsequent repayment. The ATO's view is that structuring such payments as loans does not change the taxable nature of the initial outflow. Key compliance messages include maintaining good records throughout the year, ensuring assets are supported by current market valuations at the start of the financial year, and engaging accountants/advisors/auditors early to ensure timely lodgement of returns.
quote: So then what they did is even though that this trustee, they ended up paying the $25,000 back a couple of years later, the ATO, they actually saw the initial payment as like a an early release benefit. So like a member lump sum and they just tax it that way. So they just text it as if you're taking money out of super. Um, and usually the tax rate on the age of 60 is is 20% plus Medicare levy. So they don't really care that you might be putting it back or that you might sort of, you know, structure it as a loan because they just think, well, you you're not supposed to have a loan. So we don't really care how you report it or whether or not you pay it back. They just, um, text you personally as a like as if you've taken the money from from super.
